title: prd-model-sla-marketplace-and-contract-exchange-2026.json
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose
This PRD describes the Model SLA Marketplace (MSE) and Contract Exchange: a product surface that lets customers purchase guaranteed serving SLAs for specific model variants and then bind those SLAs to routes, teams, or contracts. The goal is to enable predictable latency and availability guarantees, convert high-value latency/availability into discrete commercial SKUs, and enable secondary exchange semantics (transfer, escrow, and rebind) for enterprise partners.

Scope
- Product surface: Marketplace UI in Console + public REST API + billing adapter + routing integration in the serving runtime.
- Primary customers: platform teams, enterprise product teams, and channel partners requiring committed SLAs.
- Out of scope for initial launch: cross-customer resale (will support intra-tenant transfer only).

Key benefits
- Predictable per-route latency/availability for mission-critical applications.
- Monetization: explicit SLA SKUs for reserved capacity and hybrid dedicated blend.
- Operational clarity: explicit ownership, audit trail, and fallback policies when SLAs cannot be met.

Product concept and UX
- Marketplace listing: each listing is a Model SLA Offer (MSO) describing a model variant (e.g., open-llama-70b-q4f16), geographic region, capacity commitment, p99 latency target, availability SLA, and price per-hour or per-token.
- Purchase flow: self-serve checkout for small purchases; contract-assisted provisioning for multi-month commitments.
- Binding: after purchase, customers create a Contract (bind) which maps MSOs to Redwood routes or tenant IDs. Bindings auto-provision reserved capacity or tag requests for routing.
- Transfer & escrow: buyers can escrow credits when initiating a multi-party transfer (partner-assisted onboarding).

High-level architecture
- Components:
  - Marketplace service (product): catalog, pricing, purchase orchestration, contract state machine.
  - Billing adapter (finance): converts MSO purchases into billing line-items and credit reservations.
  - Routing integration (serving runtime): route-level policy that consults Contract registry to prefer bound model variants and reserved pools.
  - Provisioner (infra): orchestrates dedicated capacity or capacity reservations for purchased MSOs.
  - Audit & compliance (security): immutable contract logs and access controls.

Requirements (MUST have)
1) Catalog model offers
- Each MSO must include: model_id, variant_tag, region, p99_latency_ms, availability_pct, capacity_units (vCPU/GPU share), price_currency, price_unit (hour/token/month), sku_id.
- API example (response):
```
{
  "sku_id": "mse-openllama-70b-lowp99-eu-west-1",
  "model_id": "open-llama-70b",
  "variant_tag": "q4f16-low-latency",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "p99_latency_ms": "45",
  "availability_pct": "99.9",
  "capacity_units": "0.25-gpu",
  "price_unit": "hour",
  "price": "12.00"
}
```

2) Purchase and contract lifecycle
- Flow steps: select MSO -> choose duration and amount -> checkout -> contract issued -> provisioning -> contract active.
- Contract states: DRAFT, PENDING_PROVISION, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, TERMINATED.
- Provisioning SLA: Provisioner must attempt to satisfy ACTIVE within T_provision = 120 minutes for hosted offers, 72 hours for private/dedicated offers. Failure moves to SUSPENDED with clear action items.

3) Runtime binding and routing behavior
- When a request arrives with route_id X, runtime consults Contract registry ordered by: explicit route binding -> tenant default contract -> region policy. If a bound MSO exists, runtime routes to reserved pool.
- Fallback rules: if reserved pool capacity is exhausted or degraded, runtime must automatically: 1) attempt adaptive fallback to compatible model variant with degraded SLA; 2) mark the call with a SLA_FALLBACK event, and 3) surface metrics in Console. Fallback must not change billing semantics for the bound contract for the initial 30s of fallback attempts.

4) Observability, SLOs and billing linkage
- Expose per-contract metrics: provision_time, p99_observed_latency_ms, availability_pct_observed, fallback_rate, utilization.
- SLO targets for MSE product: p99_observed_latency_ms <= offered_p99 + 5ms (target 90% of time per billing period), availability_pct_observed >= offered_availability - 0.2% (measured monthly).
- Billing adaptation: if observed metrics fall below thresholds for a billing period, customers receive standardized crediting: (downtime_seconds / total_seconds) * monthly_contract_value capped at 20%.

5) API and Console surfaces
- REST endpoints required (examples):
  - GET /v1/mse/offers?region={region}&model={model_id}
  - POST /v1/mse/purchase {sku_id, quantity, duration_months}
  - GET /v1/mse/contracts/{contract_id}
  - POST /v1/mse/contracts/{contract_id}/transfer {destination_tenant_id}
- Console pages: Marketplace catalog, Contract management (bindings, lifecycle), Audit trail, SLAs & credits summary.

6) Security and compliance
- All contract and purchase events must be stored in immutable append-only logs (retention 7 years for enterprise customers on Private deployments).
- Role-based access controls: only Contract Admins can create bindings. Read-only roles may see SLA metrics but not transfer control.

7) Pricing and packaging model (initial)
- Two SKUs: Reserved-Hourly (hourly billed reserved capacity) and Monthly-Commit (discounted monthly contract).
- Pricing examples (illustrative):
  - Reserved-Hourly: open-llama-7b q6a priority p99-100ms -> $3.50/hour per 0.1-gpu share.
  - Monthly-Commit 6mo: 30% discount off list hourly * committed hours.
- Add-on: Premium SLAs include SRE-assisted provisioning and a 1-hour critical response SLA (separately contracted).

8) Edge cases and constraints
- Private/on-prem bundles: MSE supports only contract issuance; provisioning must be manual or via Onprem Provisioner.
- Model compatibility: Market offers will be curated; unsupported or custom models require manual onboarding.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs)
- Marketplace API 99.9% uptime.
- Purchase latency (checkout) < 5s for under-100-item carts.
- Catalog query P99 < 100ms for cached responses.

Metrics of success (KPIs)
- 6 months after launch: $X M ARR from MSE (target to be set by GTM).
- Customer adoption: 20 enterprise contracts signed within 90 days of launch.
- Operational: Average provisioning time <= 60 minutes for hosted MSOs.

Rollout plan
- Phase 0 (Q3 2026) - Alpha (internal + 2 pilot customers): core catalog, purchase flow, contract lifecycle, runtime binding to dev pools.
- Phase 1 (Q4 2026) - Beta (selected customers): add billing adapter, Console listing, SLA observability, limited regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1).
- Phase 2 (Q1 2027) - GA: full catalog, partner portal, monthly commits, cross-team transfers, formal SLAs in terms of credits.
- Rollout checklist (sample):
  1) Finalize SKU taxonomy and legal contract template (Product + Legal).
  2) Implement billing adapter and test reconciliation (Finance).
  3) Provisioning playbook and runbook (Infra + SRE).
  4) Security review and penetration test (Security).
  5) Pilot with 2 customers and measure provisioning and p99 compliance (CS + Solutions).

Operational playbooks and runbooks
- Provisioning failure runbook summary:
  1) Detect failed provision within 120 minutes -> alert on oncall SRE team (pager).
  2) Move contract to SUSPENDED and notify contract owner with playbook link.
  3) Options: a) manual provisioning (exec provisioner) b) migrate binding to alternate compatible MSO (customer opt-in) c) refund/credit flow initiation.
- SLA credit calculation snippet (pseudocode):
```
credit = min(monthly_value * 0.20, monthly_value * (downtime_seconds / total_seconds))
```

Billing and accounting notes
- Billing adapter must create line-items with fields: invoice_id, contract_id, sku_id, start_time, end_time, billable_units, unit_price, credit_adjustments.
- Finance must reconcile revenue recognition: reserved hourly revenue recognized ratably over provisioning window.

Open questions (to resolve before Beta)
- Q1: What is the maximum customer-visible credit cap for repeated SLA misses across multiple months? (proposed cap 20%).
- Q2: Should fallback calls be billed at the contracted rate or the executed model rate after a 30s grace period? (proposed: contracted rate for first 30s; executed model rate thereafter).
- Q3: Interoperability with Dedicated capacity reservations already sold by Sales (mapping strategy).

Appendices
- API examples
GET catalog example:
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/mse/offers?region=us-west-2&model=open-llama-70b'
```
POST purchase example:
```
curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"sku_id":"mse-openllama-70b-lowp99-us-west-2","quantity":4,"duration_months":3}' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/mse/purchase'
```
- Contract state machine (table):
| State | Allowed actions | Owner | Notes |
| DRAFT | edit, submit | customer | pre-provisioning |
| PENDING_PROVISION | cancel, retry | provisioning | in progress |
| ACTIVE | suspend, terminate, transfer | customer / admin | live & billable |
| SUSPENDED | resolve, terminate | infra / customer | failed provisioning or SLA incident |
| TERMINATED | archive | system | final state |

- Legal template pointers: reference clause IDs for credits, force majeure, and change of control in contract templates.
